paras.text: Adjuster and Public Adjuster Licensing, Chapter Twelve of the Michigan Insurance Code, Audio Lecture

This is the domain that governs who may adjust an insurance claim in Michigan, who may charge a fee for helping a homeowner with a claim, and what happens to a contractor or public adjuster who steps over the line.

I want to tell you plainly why this chapter matters more to you than any other one in this track. It is the reason a restoration contractor cannot also be the person negotiating the claim. And it is the reason you cannot hold a Michigan adjuster license while you are connected to a restoration company. Not because of anything you did. Because of a sentence in a statute that closes the door before conduct is ever discussed.
So learn this one carefully. Fourteen ideas. After most of them, a question and silence. Answer out loud.
Idea one. The shape of Chapter Twelve.
Chapter Twelve of the Insurance Code of nineteen fifty six, Act two eighteen, runs from M C L five hundred point twelve hundred through twelve forty seven.

It licenses four kinds of people in one chapter. Insurance producers, who you would call agents. Solicitors. Adjusters. And insurance counselors. All four touch an insurance transaction for pay, which is the common thread holding one chapter around four different jobs.
Twelve hundred through twelve forty seven. That is the range everything below lives inside.
Idea two. The first trap, and it is a strange one. The key words are never defined.

If you go looking for a definition of the word adjuster, or the phrase adjuster for the insured, which is Michigan's own term for what every other state calls a public adjuster, you will not find one.
M C L five hundred point twelve zero one is the definitions section. It defines agent, agent of the insured, agent of the insurer, insurance producer, negotiate, sell, and solicit.
It does not define adjuster. It does not define adjuster for the insured. It does not define independent adjuster.
Those are operative words used throughout the chapter without ever being pinned down.

And D I F S's own paperwork stumbles on the same gap. In one of the cases we will cover, D I F S pointed to two sections for the phrase fire repair contractor, and those sections actually define good moral character, not that phrase at all.

So when you meet these terms, understand what you are doing. You are reconstructing their meaning from how they are used, not reading a clean definition. That is an uncomfortable place to stand, and it is where the law actually leaves you.
Idea three. Section twelve twenty two, subsection one. Three triggers, not one.
This is the whole ballgame section.

M C L five hundred point twelve twenty two, subsection one, says a person shall not adjust loss or damage under a policy of insurance, or advertise, solicit business, or hold himself or herself out to the public as an adjuster, unless he or she is licensed as an adjuster.
Notice there are three separate triggers packed into one sentence.
Actually adjusting a loss is one. Advertising as an adjuster is a second. And just holding yourself out as one, even without a single claim file in hand, is a third.

Hear what that means. You do not have to touch a claim to violate this section. Offering the service is enough. A website, a business card, a sentence in a sales conversation. That is the violation, standing alone.
Question. A contractor has never adjusted a claim in his life, but his website says he handles the insurance claim for you. Has he got a problem, and which trigger.
Yes. Advertising and holding himself out as an adjuster are separate triggers under twelve twenty two, subsection one. He does not need to have touched a claim.
Idea four. The five exemptions, and the sixth one that does not exist.
Subsection two lists the exemptions, and there are exactly five, lettered A through E.
Memorize the count as hard as the content, because this is where exam writers and real world contractors both love to insert a sixth that does not exist.
Letter A, a person admitted to the practice of law in this state.
Letter B, a marine average adjuster, a narrow maritime specialty.

Letter C, an employee or manager of an authorized insurer adjusting a loss under a policy that same insurer issued. That is your everyday company adjuster, exempt because of the employment relationship, not because of a separate license.
Letter D, a licensed insurance producer to whom the insurer has granted claim authority.

Letter E, a narrow data entry carve out. Someone who collects or furnishes claim information and enters it into a claims system, but only while supervised by a licensed independent adjuster or an exempt insurer employee.
That is it. Five.
There is no contractor exemption anywhere in this list.

So say the consequence out loud, because it is the practical heart of the chapter. A restoration contractor who writes an estimate, submits it to the carrier on the homeowner's behalf, and negotiates the settlement for a fee is doing exactly what this section licenses. No relabeling changes that. The only way a contractor sits inside this list is if that contractor is also a licensed Michigan attorney.
Question. Name the five exemptions, and tell me which one a restoration contractor fits into.

Attorney admitted in Michigan, marine average adjuster, the insurer's own employee or manager adjusting under that insurer's policy, a licensed producer with claim authority, and a supervised data entry person. A restoration contractor fits into none of them.
Idea five. Getting the license, under twelve twenty four.
M C L five hundred point twelve twenty four governs how you get it.
The commissioner decides a completed application within sixty days, may require a written exam, and can waive that exam for someone licensed as an adjuster within the preceding twelve months.

Subsection three lists what the commissioner checks. Reasonable understanding of the insurance being adjusted. Reasonable understanding of Michigan insurance law. Good faith intent. Good business reputation. And good moral character.
Five checks in subsection three. Hold that number, because in a few minutes it is going to matter which subsection a real case was charged under.
Idea six. Subsection four. The sentence that closes your door.
This is the one this entire domain revolves around, so here it is close to verbatim.

The commissioner shall not issue a license to act as an adjuster to a person who is employed by, owns stock in, is an officer or director of, or in any other manner is connected with, a fire repair contractor.
Count the hooks in that sentence. There are four. Employment. Stock ownership. An officer or director title. And that broad catch all, in any other manner is connected with.

Now understand what kind of rule this is, because the category matters more than the words. This is a licensing bar, not a conduct standard. It stops the commissioner from ever issuing the license in the first place, before any misconduct is even alleged.

That is why you cannot hold a Michigan adjuster license today. It is not about how you would behave. Any role with a restoration contractor, ownership, an officer title, or that catch all connection, closes the door before conduct ever comes into question.
And notice how wide that fourth hook is. In any other manner is connected with does not have edges you can engineer around. That is the point of writing it that way.
Question. What are the four hooks in twelve twenty four, subsection four, and is it about what you did or about who you are connected to.

Employed by, owns stock in, is an officer or director of, or in any other manner is connected with a fire repair contractor. It is about the connection, not about conduct. It is a bar on issuing the license at all.
Idea seven. Twelve twenty six, and the rules for the contract itself.
M C L five hundred point twelve twenty six has four pieces.
First, an adjuster for the insured cannot pay someone to help solicit or adjust a loss unless that person is both regularly employed by the adjuster and separately licensed. Both, not either.

Second, when soliciting, the adjuster must orally identify as an adjuster for the insured and leave a card stating that title and their rates. And they cannot claim to be an insurer's adjuster, a fire investigator, or connected to a fire department.
Third, the number you must know cold. An adjuster for the insured shall not charge a rate exceeding ten percent of the amount paid by the insurer in settlement of the loss.

D I F S's own guidance adds a wrinkle worth having. That ten percent applies only to the coverages actually marked on the contract. So a public adjuster hired for building and contents cannot also take ten percent of a loss of use payment the contract never covered.

Fourth, and this is the piece that generates the most litigation. An adjuster for an insured shall not provide services to a client until there is a written contract, on a form approved by the commissioner. And a contract signed within forty eight hours of the loss is voidable at the insured's option for ten days after signing. A copy must be given to the insured at signing.

Three separate requirements inside that fourth piece. The approved form. The forty eight hour and ten day voidability window. And the copy requirement. Skip any one of them and you are exposed. Remember that, because a case in a few minutes turns on exactly this.
Ten percent, forty eight hours, ten days. Those are the three numbers.
Idea eight. Twelve twenty seven, the conduct companion.
A companion conduct section, twelve twenty seven, adds three rules.
No soliciting a loss while it is still happening or while fire department personnel are on scene.

No collecting a fee from a repair contractor for steering repair work to that contractor. That is the statutory wall against adjuster to contractor kickbacks, and it is worth knowing exactly because it describes an arrangement people propose casually.
And no advancing money to an insured while a claim is pending.
Idea nine. A different license entirely. The insurance counselor.
M C L five hundred point twelve thirty two requires a license for anyone who audits or abstracts policies, or gives advice, counsel, or opinion about a policy's benefits, coverage, terms, or value.
Here is the trap, and it runs the opposite direction from what people fear.
The second sentence says a non licensee shall not use terms such as consultant or consulting services, or any other language, in a way which implies that he or she is a licensed insurance counselor.

Read that conditionally, because it is written conditionally. The word ban depends on the implication of licensure. It is not an outright ban on the word consultant showing up anywhere near an insurance sentence.

So people spend their worry on the wrong sentence. The much bigger exposure sits in the first sentence. Writing a claim estimate for every dollar owed and submitting it to a carrier is advice about the value of the policy, and that is licensed territory regardless of what you call the fee.
Attorneys are exempt from this section too, same as they are from the adjuster license requirement.
And a companion section, M C L five hundred point twelve thirty six, requires a signed written fee agreement in advance of any counselor service, retained for at least two years.
Idea ten. Discipline, and the emergency lever.
M C L five hundred point twelve forty two is the procedural engine.
The commissioner must give written notice with a hearing right before refusing a license, and may suspend or revoke after notice and a hearing for failing to maintain standards or violating the act.
Subsection four is the emergency lever. Without any prior hearing, the commissioner may summarily suspend a license if protection of the public requires emergency action.
If a hearing is then requested, it must happen within twenty days, and a decision must be announced within thirty days after that hearing concludes.
Twenty days to the hearing, thirty days to the decision. A pair, in that order.
Idea eleven. The money, under twelve forty four.
M C L five hundred point twelve forty four is where the dollar amounts live, and there are two tiers plus a separate tier for defiance.

After a hearing, the director can order a civil fine of not more than one thousand dollars per violation. That rises to not more than five thousand dollars per violation if the person knew or should have known they were violating the chapter. Capped at fifty thousand dollars total per order.
The director can also order a refund of overcharges, restitution to the insured, and suspension or revocation of the license.
And if someone then knowingly violates a resulting cease and desist order, the stakes go up again. Up to twenty thousand dollars per violation, capped at one hundred thousand dollars per order.
One thousand ordinary, five thousand knowing, fifty thousand cap. Then twenty thousand and one hundred thousand for defying the order. Two pairs.
Question. Knowing violation, what is the per violation fine and the cap on the order, and what happens if he then ignores the cease and desist.

Five thousand dollars per violation, capped at fifty thousand per order. Knowingly violating the resulting cease and desist order runs up to twenty thousand per violation, capped at one hundred thousand per order.
Idea twelve. Guldshtadt, where all of this actually happened to somebody.
The first real case is Aleksandr Guldshtadt, D I F S enforcement case number twenty five dash one eight three five zero.
He was a licensed non resident adjuster for the insured, affiliated with a firm called Nationwide Insurance Claims Advocates.

D I F S summarily suspended his license on November third, twenty twenty five, using that emergency authority in twelve forty two, subsection four. His final decision came down April first, twenty twenty six. License revoked, and a fifty thousand dollar civil fine, sitting right at the statutory cap.

What did D I F S find? He was listed as C E O of a California general contractor whose website advertised fire restoration, on that company's California corporate filings, and as its registered agent on the Michigan filings, even though he told a D I F S investigator he did not partner with contractors.
That is the connected with a fire repair contractor problem, in the flesh.
Now here is a precision point worth carrying, because it shows the statute working in two different ways.

The categorical licensing bar is twelve twenty four, subsection four. But D I F S did not charge him under it. Because he was already licensed, D I F S ran the charge through twelve twenty four, subsection three, and twelve forty two, subsection two. Failure to maintain the standards required for initial licensing.

Know both routes. The text bar for an applicant. The maintenance route for a sitting licensee. Subsection four keeps you from getting it. Subsection three plus twelve forty two takes it away once you have it.

He also entered more than twenty five public adjusting contracts before D I F S ever approved his contract form, many of them carrying a thirty five percent fee. That is more than triple the ten percent cap. And he used unlicensed individuals to present those contracts to homeowners.

One important detail about how much weight this decision carries. Guldshtadt never requested a hearing, so the whole decision rests on a default record. Unchallenged allegations accepted as true, not findings tested in a contested hearing. That does not make it wrong. It does mean you should describe it accurately.
Idea thirteen. Tredenick, and an eight percent fee that vanished.

The second case is Tredenick versus Nationwide Agribusiness, involving a public adjuster called Prime Adjusting Service. Michigan Court of Appeals number three four nine eight eight seven, decided April eighth, twenty twenty one.

Label it correctly before you use it. This one is unpublished and per curiam, which means under the court rules it is persuasive only, not binding precedent. Even though it is the clearest applied reading we have of that forty eight hour and ten day rule.
Here is what happened. After a farm fire, a licensed public adjuster signed an eight percent contract with the Tredenicks.

The form Prime used was not a D I F S approved form. It omitted the forty eight hour, ten day voidability sentence. It also lacked the Home Solicitation Sales Act three day cancellation notice, though the Court of Appeals decided the case on the insurance code defect alone.

Now watch the timing, because it is the entire point of the case. That contract was actually signed about a month after the fire. So the missing forty eight hour clause could not have helped these homeowners on these facts.
And the court held that made no difference at all.

The trial court let the Tredenicks void the contract, and denied the adjuster both its eight percent fee and a fallback claim for quantum meruit, which is payment for the reasonable value of services actually performed even without an enforceable contract.

The Court of Appeals affirmed both denials. Its key line is worth memorizing: given that the adjuster failed to meet the statutory condition precedent to perform public adjuster services, there is no inequity in denying it payment for those services.

One small warning if you ever quote that line in writing. The opinion as published actually prints the word i n h e r i t, not inherent. So quote it exactly or paraphrase it, but never silently fix a court's text.

Read the holding straight through, because the result is brutal and instructive. A licensed adjuster, on a modest eight percent contract, with a defective form, recovered nothing. Not the contract price. Not a fallback payment.

That is the baseline for measuring any percentage fee claim by an unlicensed party on a Michigan property loss. If a licensed adjuster with a paperwork defect gets zero, think about where an unlicensed contractor stands.
Question. The form defect could not have hurt these particular homeowners, because they signed a month after the fire. Why did the adjuster still lose everything.

Because compliance with the statute is a condition precedent to performing the services at all. It is not a harm based test. The court found no inequity in denying payment, and denied the eight percent fee and quantum meruit both.
Idea fourteen. Florida, strictly as contrast, and the exam logistics.

Florida's public adjuster statute defines a public adjuster as anyone who prepares, completes, or files a claim, or negotiates a settlement, for value, regardless of how that person describes or presents his or her services.

That last clause is Florida's anti relabeling rule, written right into the definition. Michigan has no equivalent sentence in twelve twenty two. Michigan reaches relabeling indirectly, through that conditional word ban we covered.

Florida also gives contractors an explicit safe harbor Michigan lacks. A licensed contractor may discuss or explain a repair bid with the owner or the insurer, as long as they are doing so for the usual and customary fees stated in their own construction contract.

Michigan contractors get no comparable sentence. So the boundary here gets drawn case by case, through enforcement actions like Guldshtadt and decisions like Tredenick. That is a much less comfortable way to know where a line is.

One practical note before the recap. D I F S contracts its licensing exams to P S I Services L L C. The flat exam fee is forty one dollars, valid one year. The Public Adjuster exam is two hours, one hundred items, seventy one percent to pass. The resident application fee is fifteen dollars plus a five dollar transaction fee, and you have six months from filing to pass the exam or you reapply and pay again.

And here is an honest absence. Neither the statute nor D I F S's licensing page mentions continuing education for adjusters, unlike producers, who owe twenty four hours every two years. Neither mentions a surety bond. If a source claims otherwise, it needs a citation, because none was found here.
Time for the rapid fire recap. Fast, as a self check.

Chapter Twelve runs from twelve hundred through twelve forty seven. Twelve twenty two has exactly five exemptions, none for contractors. Twelve twenty four, subsection four, bars anyone connected with a fire repair contractor from holding the license. Twelve twenty six caps the fee at ten percent and requires the D I F S approved contract, with the forty eight hour, ten day voidability window. Twelve thirty two conditionally restricts the word consulting. Twelve forty two gives summary suspension power. Twelve forty four caps civil fines at fifty thousand dollars per order, or one hundred thousand for violating a cease and desist order. Guldshtadt lost his license and paid fifty thousand. Tredenick's adjuster lost an eight percent fee over a defective form.
Know these numbers and the five exemptions by heart. If any of the questions I asked gave you trouble, that is exactly where to drill.
